cards.title: Content creation vs. random 'posting'
cards.takeaway: Random posting talks about yourself; real content creation intentionally gives useful value (education, help, or joy) to a specific audience.
cards.body:
Anyone can upload a blurry selfie saying *'Happy Tuesday guys'* — that is just **posting**.

**Content creation** is making videos, carousels, or articles that **solve a problem, answer a question, or entertain a clear group of people** so strangers trust you, follow you, and buy from you!

cards.title: Picking a Niche — why 'my audience is everybody' fails!
cards.takeaway: When you speak to 'everybody', nobody feels you are speaking to THEM — a focused niche makes the right people follow immediately.
cards.body:
Compare two creators:
- **Too vague:** *'Lifestyle, comedy, crypto, football, and food'* → Visitors are confused and scroll past.
- **Clear Niche:** *'Affordable ₦2,000–₦5,000 healthy meals for busy Nigerian students & young workers'* → Instant follow!

Build a simple **Audience Avatar** naming three concrete things:
1. **Who** they are (age/life situation)
2. **What goal/need** they want
3. **What obstacle** stops them right now (*'young people who like nice things'* is way too vague!).

check.prompt: Why does saying 'My content is for everybody' hurt a new creator?

choices.text: Because platforms ban accounts with big audiences
Because generic content feels relevant to nobody in particular, so viewers scroll past and algorithms don't know who to show you to
Because phones run out of storage
Because niches are only for banks

check.hint: People hit Follow when they think 'Whoa, this page was made specifically for people like me!'
check.explanation: Exactly! A clear niche tells both human viewers and the platform algorithm exactly who needs your videos.

cards.title: Winning the first 3 seconds: The C-P-C Hook Pattern!
cards.takeaway: A great opening hook combines C = Curiosity, P = Problem (or Promise), and C = Clarity in the very first line!
cards.body:
On TikTok, Reels, and YouTube, viewers decide whether to swipe away in **2–3 seconds**. Saying *'Fashion video, watch it'* has zero curiosity and zero value!

Use the **C-P-C Hook Formula**:
- **C — Curiosity:** Spark an open question in their mind.
- **P — Problem or Promise:** Name the pain they feel or the win they will get.
- **C — Clarity:** Make the topic unmistakable right away.

*Strong C-P-C example:*
> *"If buying lunch finishes your salary by the 10th (**Problem**), this ₦1,500 meal-prep plate (**Clarity**) will save your month (**Promise + Curiosity**)."*

check.prompt: What do the three letters in the C-P-C Hook Pattern stand for?
check.hint: Make them curious (C), touch their pain or goal (P), and be clear what the video is about (C)!
check.explanation: Boom! Curiosity + Problem/Promise + Clarity stops the scroll without resorting to misleading clickbait.

cards.title: Content Pillars — never wake up asking 'What do I post today?'
cards.takeaway: Choose 3–4 repeatable Content Pillars (recurring sub-topics inside your niche) so brainstorming ideas takes 5 minutes a week.
cards.body:
**Content pillars** are 3 to 4 repeatable buckets inside your niche. For example, a Port Harcourt baker's 3 pillars might be:
1. **Quick baking tips** (educational)
2. **Behind-the-scenes cake decorating** (satisfying proof)
3. **Pricing & cake ordering mistakes to avoid** (buyer trust)

Rotating through 3 pillars keeps your page focused **and** gives you endless post ideas!

check.prompt: Why is the hook 'Fashion video, watch it' weak, and how does C-P-C fix it?

choices.text: It is too long; make it just 'Video'
It sparks zero curiosity and names no viewer problem or benefit — e.g. 'Stop ironing native wear wrong: 3 tricks to stay crisp all Sunday' fixes both!
Viewers only read hashtags, not hooks

check.hint: Give the viewer a clear reason *why* watching the next 30 seconds helps them!
check.explanation: 100% right! Naming a specific problem/benefit with curiosity and clarity turns passive scrollers into eager viewers.
